decisions.quote: In the present study, we indeed found more activation in the social dynamic compared to the non-social dynamic condition, indicated by significantly larger HbO increase in the posterior temporal region in the social dynamic condition. We thus replicated the findings of  Lloyd-Fox et al.’s study (2009) . However, while  Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009)  reported bilateral activation in five-month olds, the HbO increase we observed for social-dynamic compared to non-social dynamic stimuli was only significant in the right hemisphere.
decisions.reason: Under the codebook hierarchy, confirming the focal effect that the paper set out to test ('Our results replicate those of Lloyd-Fox et al.' in the abstract, where bilateral activation is not mentioned, and 'In the present study, we indeed found more activation... We thus replicated the findings of Lloyd-Fox et al.’s study (2009)' opening the discussion) is one comparison rather than a post-contrast Rule 1 overall verdict on the whole replication that outweighs a stated contrast. In the primary statistical analysis (Methods 2.4 and Results 3.2, Table 1), the authors explicitly re-tested the social-dynamic versus non-social-dynamic contrast across bilateral posterior temporal channels (Left H channels 7–10 and Right H channels 17–20) where Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009) had reported bilateral activation. They found a significant HbO increase only in the right hemisphere (channel 18) and in no left-hemisphere channels, and explicitly contrasted this tested finding with the original in the Discussion ('However, while Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009) reported bilateral activation in five-month olds, the HbO increase we observed for social-dynamic compared to non-social dynamic stimuli was only significant in the right hemisphere'). Although a follow-up direct inter-hemispheric lateralization test was only marginally significant (p = 0.05) so strong conclusions about lateralization as a developmental mechanism could not be drawn, a pre-specified tested finding that the paper itself contrasts with the original cannot be left out of the verdict and yields a 'mixed' outcome under Rule 2.

decisions.quote: Our results replicate those of Lloyd-Fox et al. and confirmed that five-to-eight-month-old infants show cortical specialization for social perception.
decisions.reason: The authors state an explicit overall verdict on the replication as a whole in both the abstract and discussion that their results replicate Lloyd-Fox et al. (2009). Under Rule 1 and the mixed-outcome rules, this overall verdict on the replication as a whole governs over the discussion's observation that the significant differential HbO increase was right-lateralized rather than bilateral.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply treats abstract Our results replicate those of Lloyd-Fox et al. as overall verdict. Full Discussion immediately says We thus replicated the findings...However while Lloyd-Fox2009 reported bilateral activation, our effect only significant in right hemisphere, then says lateralization analysis marginal and no strong conclusions. Codebook explicitly says opening confirmation of focal effect does not outweigh a tested-original contrast unless truly overall verdict on whole replication. Decide whether lateralization is an explicitly contrasted re-tested finding (mixed), a non-conclusive incidental observation authors do not treat as replication failure (successful), or evidence insufficient. Do not decide merely by significance or treat any use of replicate as overall. Read actual original-specific discussion/abstract and main claim. State how codebook hierarchy applies.

parent_source_inspection.note: Original-specific quote and surrounding source inspected.304finalscope distinguishes focal social-activation success from explicitly retested bilateral contrast; mixed accepted under codebook, not inferred from significance alone.
